questions.stem: A reply to a policy question is confident and wrong. The right passage was not among the chunks the model was given. Which first step fits?

options.text: Lower the temperature so the wording stops varying
options.says: Ruled out because "Sampling settings change how an answer is worded and not what evidence it was given".

options.text: Move the question to a larger model that knows more
options.says: Ruled out because "A larger model does not know a document it was never shown".

options.text: Inspect the index and how the documents are split
options.says: The evidence was never retrieved, so the index and the splitting of documents are the cheapest place to look.

options.text: Add examples of confident replies to the prompt
options.says: Ruled out because "Examples teach a format; they do not supply a missing fact".

origin.section: Diagnosing a wrong answer in the order that is cheapest to check

questions.stem: A team's check for its research agent demands exactly three searches in a fixed order, and it fails runs that reach the right answer by another route. What should the check judge instead?

options.text: Whether the runs repeated the same steps, because identical steps prove reliability
options.says: Ruled out because "an eval that checks for a prescribed sequence of steps fails correct runs".

options.text: Whether the outcome is correct, then whether the process was sensible
options.says: "Even with identical starting points, agents might take completely different valid paths to reach their goal", so the rule is "Check that the result is right, then check that the process was reasonable".

options.text: The number of tool calls, since fewer calls mean a better agent
options.says: Ruled out because tool efficiency is only one of "five criteria (factual accuracy, citation accuracy, completeness, source quality and tool efficiency)".

options.text: The final text, without any look at how it was reached
options.says: Ruled out because the rule is to "check that the process was reasonable" after the result.

origin.section: Mixed methods: one grader per kind of output

questions.stem: A team delays building graded examples until it can afford several hundred of them, and early prompt changes are judged by feel. What does the research team's experience suggest?

options.text: Test on the examples written in the prompt
options.says: Ruled out because the set should "mirror your real-world task distribution", and "The examples written into a prompt are not that distribution".

options.text: Wait until the full set has been built
options.says: Ruled out because "We often hear that AI developer teams delay creating evals because they believe that only large evals with hundreds of test cases are useful", which the team found untrue.

options.text: Judge by feel until launch, then measure
options.says: Ruled out because "every week without an eval is a week of judging by feel".

options.text: Start now with a small set of real queries
options.says: Early changes are large, so a small set shows them.

origin.section: Metrics, evaluation sets and where a headline hides the failure
